The standard lodging cap is USD 250 per night before taxes and fees, covering the room rate only. Local occupancy taxes, resort fees and mandatory service charges are reimbursable above the cap.

The cap rises to USD 350 per night in Boston, New York, San Francisco, London, Zurich and Tokyo, and for any city during a period when a conference the company is attending has inflated local rates.

Where the standard cap cannot be met due to limited availability, you book the most reasonable available option and note the reason. No pre-approval is needed.

Next steps:

- Note the reason if you exceed the cap

A stay of more than 30 consecutive days in another country requires approval from three separate sources: your director, Tax & Legal, and your direct manager. All three approvals must be in place before departure.

Tax & Legal must conduct a review to determine whether shadow payroll must be opened, whether a certificate of coverage is needed for social security, and whether your planned activities create permanent-establishment exposure.

Tax & Legal review requests must be filed at least 21 calendar days before departure. The request names the destination, exact dates, workspace address, and a description of the work you will perform while abroad.

The review outcome is one of three: Approved (trip proceeds as requested), Approved with conditions (trip proceeds with named restrictions, often prohibiting customer-facing activity and setting a hard end date), or Not approved (the exposure cannot be managed at reasonable cost, and you are offered an alternative destination or shorter stay).

Next steps:
- File Tax & Legal review request 21+ days before departure
- Obtain director and direct manager approvals
- Confirm all three approvals are recorded before travel

Company laptops are refreshed on a 36-month cycle. MosaicOne opens a refresh ticket automatically 60 days before the anniversary, and IT arranges the swap at a time you choose.

A refresh that falls due on the cycle is an IT ticket and nothing else: no spending approval is raised, whatever the replacement machine costs, because a refresh replaces standard issue rather than adding to it.

All company equipment must be returned within 5 business days of the final day of employment.

As a hybrid employee, you must work on site at least 3 days each week. The specific days are set by your team to ensure collaborative overlap, with most teams anchoring on Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday.

The requirement is measured as a rolling four-week average in MosaicOne rather than week by week, so a single unusual week is never a compliance problem. Weeks containing company holidays, approved PTO or approved travel reduce the requirement proportionally.

Next steps:

PTO requests must be submitted at least 5 business days in advance. A request of six or more consecutive business days requires 15 business days of advance notice. Notice is counted in business days between the day the request is submitted in MosaicOne and the first day of the requested absence, excluding both the submission day and any company holiday on your office calendar.

Your direct manager, Dana, approves PTO requests up to 5 consecutive business days with 5 business days' notice. Requests of 6 to 15 consecutive business days also require 15 business days' notice. Requests of more than 15 consecutive business days require director approval in addition to your manager's approval.

- Submit in MosaicOne at least 5–15 business days ahead.
